reference.title: Scenario 11 — Three-level deep nested Numbered list in Procedure (Sub-steps and Options)
reference.shortdesc: Consider a procedure where the first two levels represent procedural actions, and the third level

section.p: Consider a procedure where the first two levels represent procedural actions, and the third level presents mutually exclusive options the user must choose from, rather than supporting reference details. In HTML, this third level is authored as a <ul> nested inside the <ol>.

entry.codeblock:
Configure the Server

  1. Configure the server.
    1. Select the authentication mode.
      • Local Authentication
      • LDAP Authentication
      • SAML Authentication
  2. Restart the service.

<task id="configure_the_server"> <title>Configure the Server</title> <taskbody> <steps> <step> <cmd>Configure the server.</cmd> <substeps> <substep> <cmd>Select the authentication mode.</cmd> <choices> <choice>Local Authentication</choice> <choice>LDAP Authentication</choice> <choice>SAML Authentication</choice> </choices> </substep> </substeps> </step> <step> <cmd>Restart the service.</cmd> </step> </steps> </taskbody> </task>

section.p: Result: Level 0 maps to <steps><step><cmd> and Level 1 maps to <substeps><substep><cmd>, same as a standard multi-level procedure. Level 2 <ul> items are mapped them to <choices><choice> instead of <info><ol>.
